stem:
Kiara lines up a lamp, a small ball, and a globe on her desk so the ball sits between the lamp and the globe and casts a small dark patch on only part of the globe. She asks how this models a solar eclipse.

Answer both parts.

options.text: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon comes between the Sun and Earth and blocks sunlight from a small area of Earth.
A solar eclipse occurs when Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon.
A total solar eclipse is visible everywhere on Earth's sunlit side at the same time.
A solar eclipse occurs whenever the Moon is on the Sun-facing side of Earth, even if it is not lined up to cast a shadow on Earth.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: In a solar eclipse the Moon is between the Sun and Earth and casts a shadow on only a small region of Earth, matching Kiara's lamp–ball–globe line-up.

teacher.key_rationale: Solar eclipse: Moon between Sun and Earth, shadow on a small area. Earth between Sun and Moon is a lunar eclipse. The shadow is local, not everywhere on the day side. Alignment that casts a shadow is required, not merely being Sun-facing.
